                    ### Question
                    A 37-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after being attacked with a knife. Physical examination shows a 4-cm laceration in the midline of the right forearm. An MRI of the right arm shows damage to a nerve that runs between the superficial and deep flexor digitorum muscles. Loss of sensation over which of the following areas is most likely in this patient?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Palmar surface of the little finger
opb. Lateral aspect of the forearm
opc. Fingertip of the index finger
opd. Medial aspect of the forearm
ope. Dorsum of the thumb

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In this scenario, the MRI indicates damage to a nerve running between the superficial and deep flexor digitorum muscles in the forearm. The median nerve is anatomically located between these muscles and is responsible for sensation in the palmar surface of the thumb, index, middle, and part of the ring finger. Therefore, damage to the median nerve would most likely result in loss of sensation in the fingertip of the index finger. The retrieved evidence supports the involvement of the median nerve, as it is part of the forearm structure and associated with numbness. The ulnar nerve, which affects the palmar surface of the little finger, is less likely involved based on the described location of the injury. The radial nerve, which affects the dorsum of the thumb, and nerves affecting the lateral and medial aspects of the forearm are unlikely to be involved given the specific location of the nerve damage. Thus, the most likely area of sensory loss is the fingertip of the index finger, aligning with the consensus on median nerve function and injury location.
